html:
The Nagarakretagama is an Old Javanese poem written in 1365 by a Buddhist court official using the pen name Prapañca. It praises Hayam Wuruk, king of Majapahit, and is the main source on that empire at its height.

It is a kakawin, a long poem in Indian metres, a form also used for the Kakawin Ramayana. Its original title, Desawarnana, means "description of the districts". It describes the capital and palace, the king's tours through East Java with lists of villages and temples, court ceremonies and the royal family tree. It also lists nearly a hundred places across the archipelago and the Malay peninsula said to pay tribute, a list modern Indonesians often read as an early outline of their country.

Gajah Mada, the chief minister, appears in it; see Gajah Mada. The manuscript that made it known was kept on Lombok. A Dutch colonial expedition took it from the palace at Cakranegara on Lombok in 1894. The Netherlands returned it to Indonesia in the 1970s, and it is now on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
